During Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) official visit at our Dahej SEZ unit (Plot No. Z/96/D, Part II), the following issues were observed: 1) Contaminated water/ wastewater found in Storm Water Drain; 2) Biomass was observed very less in aeration tank; and 3) ETP sludge is found stored in open area near ETP.

The Company has addressed and complied with the alleged non-compliances mentioned in the Directions. This has been communicated to the relevant authority, along with the necessary supporting documents. Consequently, manufacturing operations at the unit continued without interruption.

Voluntary Closure Directions u/s 33A of the water (P&CP) Act 1974 and u/s 31A of the Air (P&CP) Act 1981

On May 17, 2025, during charging of Dimethyl Sulfate solution, due to delayed stoppage of the isolation valve, approximately 10–15 kg material overflowed in the plant area. The spill spread over approximately 15 sq. ft. area and exposure was limited to workers present in the vicinity. The incident was immediately controlled and contained without significant environmental impact. Incident was related to process safety & hazardous chemical handling. Management informed all concerned authorities including Directorate of Industrial Safety and Health and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board.

Based on the incident report, Maharashtra Pollution Control Board issued voluntary closure directions for the particular activity on May 20, 2025 as a precautionary regulatory measure. The Company submitted compliance report on May 21, 2025. Further verification was carried out by the officer and based on satisfactory verification, restart permission for the activity was granted.

On February 19, 2026, due to leakage from a solvent line flange resulted in fire at a limited area at the Dahej unit. No damage or injury to any workmen was reported. However, 40 kg. approx. burnt residue generated due to the incident was disposed of through authorized manifest system and around 2.5 KL contaminated water generated during firefighting/ cleaning activity was treated at the in-house ETP and discharged to GIDC drainage system as per prescribed norms.

Based on the incident, certain directions were issued by Gujarat Pollution Control Board under Section 31A of the Air Act, 1981 which were duly complied by the Company and the action taken report was also furnished to the Gujarat Pollution Control Board along with a Bank Guarantee of ` 5 Lakh.
